issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s demand for possession on the ground of rent arrears is not waived where the tenant did not plead waiver and the landlord’s later conduct consisted only of the tenant standing surety, without payment or an agreed adjustment against rent.
material_facts: In an eviction suit based on rent arrears, the tenant was found to have defaulted for more than four months after service of a demand notice.
The tenant did not plead waiver before the trial court; the trial court raised the issue on its own.

The tenant’s asserted conduct was standing surety for the landlord’s sales-tax arrears; the tenant made no payment to the sales-tax authorities on the landlord’s behalf, and the landlord did not agree to adjust any such payment against rent.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s demand was not waived. The trial court’s contrary finding was illegal and perverse, and the eviction decree granted by the District Court was properly restored.
issues.legal_principle: A court should not decide waiver when the tenant has not pleaded it. On the facts here, merely standing surety, without payment on the landlord’s behalf or an agreed adjustment against rent, did not waive the landlord’s demand for possession. The Court relied on Section 20(2)(a) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972; it cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: arrears_ground_eviction_suit and rent_default_after_demand and waiver_not_pleaded and tenant_only_stood_surety and no_payment_or_rent_adjustment

predicates.arrears_ground_eviction_suit: The proceeding was an eviction suit relying on the tenant’s rent arrears as the ground for eviction.
predicates.rent_default_after_demand: The tenant remained in arrears for the required period after the landlord demanded payment.
predicates.waiver_not_pleaded: The tenant did not plead waiver before the trial court.
predicates.tenant_only_stood_surety: The tenant’s asserted later conduct was standing surety for the landlord’s debt.
predicates.no_payment_or_rent_adjustment: The tenant made no payment toward that debt on the landlord’s behalf, and the landlord did not agree to adjust a proposed payment against rent.

issues.definition: When an eviction suit rests on rent arrears and the tenant did not plead waiver, merely standing surety without paying the landlord’s debt or agreeing to adjust it against rent does not waive the landlord’s demand.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant is entitled to relief from eviction for rent arrears only upon satisfying the statutory requirements for payment or tender at the first hearing, including that the tender be unconditional and cover the full amount due.
material_facts: The eviction suit was brought on the ground of rent arrears.
The tenant asserted that an amount had been deposited, but the record did not establish that the deposit was made at the first hearing.
The tenant’s written statement denied that rent arrears or default existed, so the asserted deposit was not an unconditional tender to the landlord.
The record did not establish that the deposit covered the full amount calculated under the statute.
issues.conclusion: The tenant failed to establish compliance with Section 20(4) and was not entitled to relief from eviction on the rent-arrears ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20(4) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, relief from eviction on the ground in Section 20(2)(a) is available only if, at the first hearing, the tenant unconditionally pays or tenders to the landlord the entire rent and damages due, together with the prescribed interest and the landlord’s suit costs, after the permitted deduction. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: arrears_ground_eviction_suit and (deposit_at_first_hearing_unproved or not tender_unconditional or full_statutory_amount_unproved)

predicates.arrears_ground_eviction_suit: The proceeding was an eviction suit based on rent arrears.
predicates.deposit_at_first_hearing_unproved: The record did not establish that the tenant deposited or tendered the amount at the first hearing.
predicates.tender_unconditional: The tenant’s payment or tender was unconditional and made for payment to the landlord.
predicates.full_statutory_amount_unproved: The record did not establish that the amount paid or tendered covered the full sum required for statutory relief.

issues.definition: In an eviction suit based on rent arrears, the tenant is not entitled to statutory relief if the first-hearing timing, unconditional nature, or full amount of the required payment or tender is not established.
